_comment: Frozen calibration evidence for retrieval_min_similarity (Milestone 2.3 final query-quality correction, see ADR 0009). Measured against the real, already-ingested demo corpus (100 pallets/flask issues + 6 documentation excerpts) using the real BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 model via fastembed 0.8.0, with the official BGE query instruction ('Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: ') applied to the query side only, exactly as app.retrieval.embedding.embed_query does, and with the query text built by the real, current production app.retrieval.stage.build_query_text (issue title + bounded body excerpt + deduplicated matched keywords only — no severity/rationale/proposed-action/label boilerplate). Scores are cosine similarity (1 - cosine distance) read directly from the already-stored passage embeddings compared against freshly computed query embeddings. This supersedes the 2026-09-16 snapshot measured against the earlier, boilerplate-including query builder, which is why every score here differs from that prior fixture. This is a small (~8-pair), one-time snapshot, not a full evaluation harness (Milestone 2.5) — see 'known_limitations'. All similarity scores in this file are frozen, previously-measured real-model output; nothing in this file is regenerated by the evaluation harness (app.evaluation), which only replays the deterministic confidence-band/discriminative-term decision against these frozen scores and the bounded query_text/candidate_text fields below — it never re-embeds, re-queries pgvector, or downloads the model.
query_builder: app.retrieval.stage.build_query_text (issue-specific content only: normalized title + bounded body excerpt + deduplicated matched keywords)
measured_against: live demo database (100 issues + 6 documents, already ingested)

positive_examples.description: Confirmed real near-duplicate: 'Flask cannot find /security/logic API' vs '404 Flask cannot find /security/login API'.
Literal duplicate title+body ('AI Junk' / 'LLM junk removed').
Literal duplicate title+body ('AI Junk' / 'LLM junk removed').

Issue<->document pair: 'Session is not updated on redirect target endpoint in tests' vs the Sessions documentation excerpt. Below chosen_threshold on its own (see known_limitations) — kept in the fixture as measured evidence, not asserted as a retrievable positive.

negative_examples.description: 'MAX_FORM_MEMORY_SIZE not being picked up correctly' vs 'Flask documentation website does not support dark mode' — clearly unrelated topics. Strongest measured issue<->issue negative.
'Flask documentation website does not support dark mode' vs 'Session is not updated on redirect target endpoint in tests' — unrelated.

'MAX_FORM_MEMORY_SIZE...' vs the Sessions documentation excerpt — unrelated, but scores *higher* than the one measured issue<->document positive (0.6153). This is the known issue<->document overlap — see known_limitations. A normalized-lexical-overlap check was also measured for this pair and did not resolve it in the expected direction (see lexical_overlap_check below), so chosen_threshold=0.65 excludes both this negative and the one measured document positive, favoring missing a weak cross-genre match over presenting unsupported evidence.

short_meaningful_query_examples.description: Shortest real meaningful (non-punctuation) issue body measured, to sanity-check the low end of the score range. Well below chosen_threshold.
Same minimal issue against a document. Well below chosen_threshold.

rejected_before_embedding_examples.description: Punctuation-only issue-specific content. Rejected by has_sufficient_query_content before any embedding call or database query — confirmed via adapter.calls == [] equivalent live check (zero embedding calls observed).

lexical_overlap_check._comment: Measured normalized Jaccard overlap of extract_meaningful_terms(query) vs extract_meaningful_terms(candidate content) for the one ambiguous issue<->document pair, to evaluate whether a blanket lexical-overlap rule could resolve it. It could not: the signal ran backwards (the negative pair had *higher* lexical overlap than the positive pair) — this is a separate, earlier finding from the two-band false-positive correction below, and is why a *blanket* lexical requirement was rejected in favor of the medium-confidence-band-only rule using *discriminative* (non-generic) terms.

false_positive_regression_examples._comment: Milestone 2.3 false-positive correction (Jesse's visible demo, 2026-09-15): the prior single close-case margin [0.65, 0.70) was too narrow — issue:5942 scored 0.7404 against issue:5755, above the old 0.70 ceiling, so it bypassed lexical confirmation and was accepted on semantic score alone despite being topically unrelated. Replaced with two bands: [min_similarity, high_confidence_similarity) requires a shared *discriminative* term (app.retrieval.query_terms.extract_discriminative_terms — meaningful terms minus corpus-generic terms and standalone numbers); >= high_confidence_similarity accepts on semantic score alone. All scores below are real, previously measured against the real demo corpus with the real production build_query_text/BGE model -- never regenerated by the evaluation harness. query_text and each example's candidate_text are the exact bounded, real strings that produced the recorded shared_discriminative_terms (first verified live during the Milestone 2.3 correction and pinned by tests/test_retrieval_calibration.py::test_discriminative_terms_extraction_matches_the_frozen_regression_evidence) -- app.evaluation replays app.retrieval.service._confidence_decision / _shared_discriminative_terms against exactly these strings and the frozen score, so the recorded decision is re-derived from the real decision function on every run, not merely trusted as a stored label.
false_positive_regression_examples.query_text: Flask cannot find /security/logic API We are using airflow 2.8.4, and recently we upgrade it to 2.10.5 Environment for Airflow 2.8.4 - Python version: 3.10 - Flask version: ``` Flask-AppBuilder==4.5.2 Flask-Babel==2.0.0 Flask-Bcrypt==1.0.1 Flask-Caching==2.3.0 Flask-JWT-Extended==4.7.1 Flask-Limiter==3.10.1 Flask-Login==0.6.3 Flask-SQLA

examples.description: Confirmed real near-duplicate. Above high_confidence_similarity (0.90) — accepted on semantic score alone, no lexical support required.
examples.candidate_text: 404 Flask cannot find /security/login API We are using airflow 2.8.4, and recently we upgrade it to 2.10.5

examples.description: 'Flask cannot find /security/logic API' vs 'Modern CSRF Protection Using Sec-Fetch-Site Header' — plausibly related through a shared security-protection subject. Medium-confidence band; accepted because 'security' is a genuine shared discriminative term (not corpus-generic — measured document frequency 4.0% in the demo corpus, well under the 10% generic cutoff).
examples.candidate_text: Modern CSRF Protection Using Sec-Fetch-Site Header Flask's documentation states that CSRF protection requires a form validation framework, necessitating one-time tokens stored in cookies for security

examples.description: 'Flask cannot find /security/logic API' vs 'flask run should support pep723' (an unrelated packaging/tooling request) — the reported false positive. Medium-confidence band; rejected because the two issues share zero discriminative terms (only the corpus-generic word 'flask' overlaps, which does not count as support).
examples.candidate_text: flask run should support pep723 Because no one wants to use: native pkgutil-style, declarative, non-declarative, setup.py, setup.cfg, pyproject.toml, pep517, setuptools, build, pip, namespace packages

examples.description: 'Flask cannot find /security/logic API' vs '3.1.2 regression: stream_with_context triggers teardown_request() calls before response generation' — a completely unrelated request-lifecycle bug. A second false positive caught during THIS correction's own live verification: an earlier, incomplete draft of the corpus-generic term list omitted 'environment' and 'version' despite both measuring above the 10% document-frequency cutoff, so #5804 was briefly accepted on nothing but shared bug-report-template boilerplate ('Environment for Airflow 2.8.4' / 'Python version: 3.10' appears near-verbatim in nearly every issue in this corpus). Fixed by completing the generic-term list to match its own documented cutoff; #5804 now correctly shares zero discriminative terms with #5755.
examples.candidate_text: 3.1.2 regression: stream_with_context triggers teardown_request() calls before response generation Hello, I believe the changes to stream_with_context() introduced a bug where the teardown_request() callables are invoked too early in the request/response lifecycle

examples.description: 'Flask cannot find /security/logic API' vs 'Test failures with click 8.3.1' — an unrelated dependency-version test-failure report. A third false positive caught during this correction's own live verification: 'using' (a common gerund of 'to use') measured only 5.7% document frequency in the demo corpus, below the 10% corpus-generic cutoff, yet still carries no discriminative concept on its own in any corpus. Fixed by adding a small, bounded, general (not corpus-frequency-derived) low-content-word set covering personal pronouns, modal verbs, and hedge adverbs alongside the corpus-measured generic terms (see app.retrieval.query_terms._LOW_CONTENT_TERMS); #5836 now correctly shares zero discriminative terms with #5755.
examples.candidate_text: Test failures with click 8.3.1 Click 8.3.1 was tagged but not released on PyPI. Running flask's test suite with that version results in test session failures using pytest 8.4.2 with 490 items collected

examples.description: 'Flask cannot find /security/logic API' vs 'AI junk' (a demo-corpus filler issue that genuinely discusses real security vulnerabilities). Medium-confidence band; accepted because 'security' is a genuine shared discriminative term -- but this is a DIFFERENT sense of 'security' than #5755's URL-path name ('/security/logic'), a real, disclosed polysemy limitation (see known_limitations and ADR 0009/0011). This example is a known, nonblocking limitation in the evaluation harness -- never asserted as a required correct match.
examples.candidate_text: AI junk Multiple security vulnerabilities in Flask: CRITICAL code execution via exec() in config.py, HIGH path traversal in several locations.

corpus_generic_terms_measurement._comment: Document frequency of each generic term across the demo corpus's 405 retrieval_chunks, measured 2026-09-15, and of a few genuinely topical words kept for comparison (not excluded). extract_discriminative_terms excludes every term at or above 10% document frequency, plus 'issue'/'project' by explicit domain-generic addendum (see app.retrieval.query_terms for the full rationale) — both measured well under 10% here precisely because chunk body text rarely spells out the word describing itself. 'environment' and 'version' are included here deliberately: an earlier, incomplete draft of this list omitted them despite both measuring above the 10% cutoff, and live verification caught the resulting false positive (issue #5804 accepted for #5755 on nothing but shared bug-report-template boilerplate) before this correction shipped.

known_limitations: issue<->issue separation is clean and well-supported: strongest measured negative 0.5750, weakest measured positive 0.9276 — a gap of about 0.35.

issue<->document separation is NOT clean: the one measured positive (0.6153) scores lower than the one measured negative (0.6239). No defensible document-specific threshold exists with this small sample. chosen_threshold=0.65 resolves this by excluding both measured document examples rather than guessing a document-specific cutoff — precision over recall for weak cross-genre matches.

A blanket lexical-overlap rule does not reliably resolve the ambiguous document pair either (see lexical_overlap_check) — this is why the medium-confidence rule requires *discriminative* terms specifically, and why high_confidence_similarity=0.90 was chosen high enough that no measured document example reaches it.

high_confidence_similarity=0.90 is provisional and based on a single confirmed near-duplicate pair (#5755/#5756) plus the two duplicate-title pairs (#6047/#6048, #6047/#6049) — more confirmed near-duplicate examples would strengthen this boundary.

The corpus-generic term list is derived from this specific 405-chunk demo corpus; a different or larger corpus would need its own document-frequency measurement (the 10% cutoff and the 'issue'/'project' addendum are the general, reusable parts of the rule).

Only a handful of issue<->document pairs total were measured — a small sample, not a statistically robust distribution. More issue<->document examples, ideally from a larger/more diverse document corpus, are needed before revisiting a document-specific threshold.
A full evaluation harness with recall/precision reporting on a larger fixed set is Milestone 2.5 scope and was not built here.
